properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the wall check has all three legs for THIS repo (script, AGENTS.md, CI) and none of the three a consumer needs (served tool, skill, detector) — and the checkout cannot feel the absence because it holds the script. The kit tarball is a symptom, not the cause
properties.statement:
① OBSERVED: on 2026-09-14 an agent on a consumer project wrote an import-boundary walk by hand and filed it through report_manual_work with diagnosis "unknown". tools/wall_check.py — built 2026-08-20 from the identical hand-rolled analysis on reflow2's own design, generalised 2026-08-21 on Anthony's word to "any project, with no configuration" — was 25 days old. Expected: the agent finds and runs it. NOT affected: the agent found report_manual_work itself, so served tools ARE findable from there.

② PRECEDENT: searched. No prior record of "a script in tools/ unreachable to consumers" — but fact:the-commands-cover-nine-of-twenty-skills-and-the-checkout-cannot-feel-it is the class (see the CAUSES edge).

③–⑤ CANDIDATES FROM THE BONES, EACH MEASURED:
  · DELIVERY (the first plausible story: "the kit tarball does not ship it"). release.yml: the kit is reflow2_init.py + getting-started/ — true, not shipped. BUT reflow2_init.py wires the loop-nudge hook by ABSOLUTE PATH into the reflow2 checkout (REPO/tools/loop_nudge.py), so an init-installed project has tools/ on disk — and would STILL not reach wall_check. Delivery alone does not explain it. Refuted as the cause; kept as a symptom.
  · FINDABILITY: find_tools indexes tool_router.list_all() — MCP tools only (query.rs). A script cannot be returned by the one search a consumer has. Measured: the user-phrased question returns evaluate_allocation, detect_defects, realizes, seam_coverage.
  · INSTRUCTION: grep of every served skill and the served instructions for wall_check — nothing. No skill names it.
  · INTENT: SATISFIES req:modularity-computed (accepted), whose statement is about the DESIGN being checkable; consumer reach was never stated as intent — it appeared only in the capability's own prose at generalisation.
  · ALLOCATION: ALLOCATED_TO cmp:structure — a SERVED component — while the only realizer is an unserved Python script. The design already disagreed with itself here and nothing read the disagreement.
  · ASSURANCE: ver:wall-check tests the script's behaviour; nothing verifies reach.
  · CHANGE: chg:wall-check-reads-the-mapping-instead-of-guessing-it generalised the CODE (reads any design's Artifact locations) and left delivery untouched.
  · GOVERNANCE/STALENESS: the capability's description claims "a reflow2 user gets this the moment they have registered artifacts" — a stale-at-birth claim nothing checked.
  · NOT IN THE SUSPECTED COMPONENT: the kit manifest (ver:kit-manifest-agrees) is checked and CORRECT — wall_check is not in it, by design. The defect is not in the kit; it is that the served surface has no entry.
  · THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: possible only if the consumer had the checkout AND a way to find the script — the second is measured absent, so the observation stands whatever the install mode.

⑥ CLASS: a capability realized by a script in this checkout, allocated to a served component, described as reaching any project, with none of the three consumer legs — and a checkout that cannot feel the absence. Would fixing the instance (ship the file) have prevented the 2026-08-14 occurrence? No. Would serving it + naming it in a skill + a gate that a capability allocated to a served component is realized by something served? Yes, for both.

⑦ PIN: a gate over the export that fails today — a Capability claiming reach beyond this repo whose only realizers are tools/ scripts — and an instance pin that find_tools returns the wall check for the coupling question. To be observed failing before the fix.

⑧ FIX at the cause: serve the wall check as an MCP tool over the live design and the working tree; name it in check-health and adopt; the gate. ⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how the consumer project was installed (kit tarball or checkout) — it does not change the cause, only whether the file was on disk; whether the other three hand-rolled analyses share this class (they do not: nothing was ever built for them — that is a different question, dec:reflow2-serves-source-reading-analyses-that-report-and-never-write).
